texts: The tortoise moves slowly, but the grindstone of deeds grinds fine, and every grain returns to the hand that fed it.
tortoise, grindstone, karma returns
My uncle cheated his partner years ago, slowly and quietly like a tortoise, and this year the grindstone of life turned and the same fate fell on his own business.
Write a doha about the tortoise that walks slowly yet surely and the grindstone that turns without haste, teaching that every deed we do, however slow to ripen, comes back to us in its full measure.
doha w a tortoise and a grindstone about how whatever u do comes back to u eventually

My brother laughed when he tricked a customer into overpaying at the weekly stall, and ten years later he fell into a debt trap himself, while a moth beat against the bulb that last night as if warning him.
doha w a moth and a well - the one who digs a well for others falls in it himself, the moth rushes to the light and gets hurt by his own wish. u know the idea
The moth that seeks the light is undone by his own longing; he who digs a well for another falls in first.
moth, well, own deeds
Please write a doha in which the one who digs a well to trap another falls into it himself, while a moth rushes to its own ruin at the light, showing that what we do to others returns to us.
Write a doha where a man standing at the crossroads is offered the paras but chooses to pass it over for a petty profit by cheating, and learns that every choice returns its fruit to the chooser.
At a crossroads of my career I could help a colleague for a modest reward or cheat him for a big bonus, a real paras moment, and my mother said whatever I choose will come back to me.
At the crossroads the paras is offered, but only the road of fair deeds brings a rich return, and the road of tricks brings its price.
doha w crossroads and the paras - every choice you make comes back as its fruit
crossroads, paras, choices
The boy who bullied me at school lost his job last year when his own manager bullied him, and my grandmother said without surprise that what you give out is what returns.
As the giver, so the receiver one day; the hand that wounds shall one day be wounded.
doha about how ur own actions come back to u, karma is real man
deeds come back
Write me a couplet that explains that every action of a person, good or bad, must in the end return to the doer, so no one should imagine that unjust deeds will pass without their consequences.
doha w a mirror and milk, what you give is what you get back, like the milk curdles if u sour it first
The mirror gives back the face that stands before it; the milk turns sour if the hand was sour. So are our deeds returned.
Write a doha in which a mirror shows each person exactly the face they bring to it and milk turns sour if mixed with something bitter, showing that what we do comes back in the form we gave.
My landlord was harsh with his tenants all his life, and when he got old his own sons would not sit beside him, and the neighbourhood said it was like a mirror, and a bitter glass of milk.
mirror, milk, deeds returned

Write a doha for the man who spoke cruel words with his tongue and then needed a physician for the harm he himself had caused, teaching that the consequences of what we say and do return to us in time.
My uncle used his sharp tongue to hurt many people, and when he fell sick and needed a physician, none of his old friends came to the hospital, and I thought, this is what comes of it.
doha with a tongue and a physician: ur mean words come back as ur problems
tongue, physician, reap
The tongue that gave the sharpest words must beg the physician for the cure; every return is of our own giving.

My neighbour set a cage for stray birds just to enjoy their noise and then was stuck indoors for months with a broken leg, and his mother used to say the winnowing fan always separates your deeds from your wishes.
winnowing fan, cage, own deeds
doha w a winnowing fan and a cage - what ur deeds are made of is what comes back sorted out for u, even the cage u built
Write a doha in which the winnowing fan separates the grain from the chaff of a man's actions and the cage he builds for others closes around him, teaching that we reap what we have made ourselves.
The winnowing fan flings the chaff away, the cage shuts on its builder; each man is bound by what his own hands have made.
My grandmother pulled the rope of the churn every morning and said that the butter is only what you put in, just like life gives back whatever you put into it.
doha w a churn and a rope - u churn what u have and u get what u put in, simple karma
Write a doha in which one pulls a rope to turn the churn, and what comes out is the result of what was poured in, to show that the fruit of our actions is exactly what we have put in.
churn, rope, deeds returned
Pull the rope as the churn turns, and know that the butter is only what was poured; so are our deeds returned.
After my sister cheated on her exams her friends stopped trusting her and she failed even the honest ones later, and our dad said that is what consequences are, not punishment, just returns.
doha about consequences of lying, like you lie once and it just comes back and bites u
Please write a doha that says every person must eat the fruit of what he has done, that no one escapes the result of his own conduct, and that those who do good will receive good in return.
None may escape the result of their own deeds; what is done in secret returns in the open.
actions have results
A man I know made his fortune by exploiting vulnerable workers, and now his children refuse to talk to him, and my grandmother simply says what you do to others finds its way home to you.
He who gives hurt shall receive hurt; he who gives kindness shall receive kindness again.
your deeds return
Write a doha for a person who thinks that hidden wrongdoings will never be repaid, explaining that the results of our actions are certain to return and cannot be bribed or escaped by anyone.
doha about getting what u deserve based on what u did
The tree in the forest bears only what its kind decreed; as the root, so the fruit, and as the deed, so the day.
doha w a tree and a forest - whatever kind of tree u plant is the fruit u get, like deeds
tree, forest, fruit of deeds
My father planted a neem tree on a barren plot when I was born, and now the whole forest-edge colony shelters under it, and he says what you give with care returns to you.

Write a doha where a tree in the forest gives fruit exactly according to its kind, nothing more and nothing different, teaching that the results of our actions are of the very nature of the deeds we did.

Give me a doha about a traveller who treated the innkeeper rudely at the inn and found every room closed against him on his return, teaching that conduct towards others comes back to the one who gave it.
doha about an inn: be nice to the host cuz what u do comes back to u next time you stay
At the inn of the world the guest who gives scorn receives cold beds; the courteous one is welcomed always.
inn, conduct returns
I was rude to the receptionist at the inn on our last trip, and this time the same woman was at the desk and gave me the worst room, and I understood the saying about reaping what you give.
Every deed leaves a silent footprint, and it walks behind you until it overtakes you at the end.
I want a doha that tells people to think before they act, because every deed they do, whether kind or cruel, will return to them as a result, and no force in the world can stop that return.
After I forgave my brother for the money he owed, he came back years later and helped me through my worst time without being asked, and my mother smiled and said goodness always makes its way back.
think before you act
doha about how good deeds come back too, not just bad ones
Write a doha about the lotus that grows in muddy water yet is untouched by it, and the one who gives kindness in an unkind place finds it blooming for him later, because good deeds return in kind.
doha with a lotus: the good u do even in a bad place blooms later for you
lotus, good deeds bloom
From the mud of hard days the lotus rises, and the kindness once given blooms back to the giver.

I volunteered at a shelter in a bad neighbourhood as a student, and years later one of those kids, now a surgeon, saved my father, and I think of the lotus pond near that shelter whenever I recall it.
cotton, moon, deeds
My aunt spun cotton by the light of the moon for the poor every winter, and when she fell ill, strangers who owed her nothing nursed her, as though her kindness had been waiting.
doha with cotton and the moon, soft kindness comes back like the moonlight returns every month
The cotton given under the moon returns as warmth in the winter of thy own need.
Compose a doha in which the soft cotton given warm to a stranger under the moon returns as a warm comfort to the giver in a time of need, to show that every kindness is repaid by life.
My cousin threw a stone at a neighbour's window as a joke, and next year somebody broke his own car window, and the whole family said, it was bound to come back.
doha with a stone: the stone u throw lands on ur own head eventually
Need a doha about a stone thrown at another that turns in the air and comes down on the thrower's own head, teaching that harm intended for others returns to its source with added force.
stone thrown, returns
The stone thou throwest at another returns in the evening to thy own head.
Write a doha for the person who believes that nobody sees their small acts of dishonesty, explaining that every act has its consequence, which will arrive even if no human eye witnessed it.
Though no eye sees thy deed, the deed sees thee; it will find thee in its own good time.
I once let a cashier's mistake in my favour pass and kept the extra change, and a month later I lost a much bigger sum in a mistake of my own, and it felt like an account being balanced.
doha about secret bad deeds still coming back to u somehow
unseen deeds return
Whatever flower thou dost give to the world, the world will one day lay back in thy hands.
Write a doha on how the good that one does for others is never lost but comes back to the doer sooner or later, so that kindness is the safest investment a person can make in the course of life.
kindness returns
My grandfather fed hungry travellers every evening for forty years, and at his funeral hundreds of strangers came to bring food to our family, and nobody had even invited them.
doha about good deeds being repaid, i keep helping people and wondering if it matters
doha w a stone and an arrow - once the arrow leaves the bow u cant take it back, same with a deed. stone too
The arrow once loosed, the stone once thrown, return not to the hand but to the fate of the one who shot.
Could you do a doha in which an arrow once shot and a stone once thrown cannot be recalled, teaching that every deed, once done, travels on to its result, and the doer must meet it in time.
I fired off a harsh email at my boss like an arrow and could not take it back, and the consequences landed on me like a stone the following week, which taught me to weigh actions first.
arrow, stone, no recall
scales, net, deeds weighed
doha w scales and a net - everything u do gets weighed in the end, and u cant escape the net of ur own deeds
The scales weigh what the net has caught; each deed is counted, and none is lost from the account.
Write a doha in which the scales weigh every deed with perfect justice and the net of consequence gathers each person's actions, teaching that no one escapes the exact result of what he has done.
The accountant at our firm weighed each expense on the scales of honest rules and caught my boss in the net of his own false entries, and I realised nobody escapes the weighing of their deeds.
At the entrance, the pot of water given to the thirsty returns as a flood of blessings.

A doha, please, in which a pot of water given freely to a thirsty stranger at the entrance comes back to the giver many times over, teaching that kindness once done never fails to return as a blessing.
door, pot, kindness returns
doha w a door and a pot of water - give the thirsty water at ur door and it comes back to u
My grandmother kept a pot of water at the door for passers-by all her life, and when she was ill, strangers she had never met arrived to help us, and the neighbours called it her returns.
Write a doha where a king builds a palace and a mosque on the tears of the poor and finds that his deeds, not his buildings, are weighed, and what he did to the poor returns upon him.
The builder who raised a palace for the minister by cheating the workers out of their wages saw his own sons disinherited, and next to the mosque the old men remarked that it all comes back.
The palace is raised, the mosque is raised, but the deed beneath them is the one that returns.
doha with a palace and a mosque - big buildings dont save u from the results of what u did
palace, mosque, reckoning
Write a doha about the swan that takes only the pure and a furnace that tests everyone, teaching that every deed passes through the test and the doer receives only what his deeds have made him.
swan, furnace, deeds tested
The swan takes the pure, the furnace burns the dross; so every deed is sifted, and returns as it is.
doha w a swan and a furnace - actions get tested in the end and u get what u deserve
The old judge in our town was known as a swan for honesty, and he sat before the furnace of public opinion without fear, saying a clean life receives only a clean reckoning.
Write a doha about a singer with a one-string lute who sings songs of hatred and finds his own shadow singing them back at him in the evening, showing that what we put into the world returns to us.
The lute plays what the fingers choose, and the shadow carries the tune home; so we hear forever what we have played.
lute, shadow, deeds follow
doha w a one-string lute and a shadow, ur deeds follow u like a shadow
My friend played hateful songs on his one-string lute in the evenings, and now his own children sing the same abuse back at him, like the shadow of a bad tune.
I'd love a doha about the date palm that bears sweet fruit high up, and the man who gave nothing and is left with nothing, teaching that only what one has given or done will be his in the end.
date palm, fruit of deeds
doha w a date palm - u get fruits only for the work ur put into it
The date palm gives its fruit to the one who tends it; the idle hand gathers nothing, as the deed so the fruit.
My uncle planted a date palm in the dry yard after he retired and everyone laughed, but twelve years later its fruit fed half the lane, and he said you only get back what you give in time.
doha w a mirror and a diamond - ur deeds polish or dull ur face like a diamond dulls with dirt, u see it in the mirror

Write a doha in which a diamond shines according to how it was cut and a mirror shows a person the face that his deeds have made, teaching that our actions shape what we become and what returns to us.
The mirror shows the face thy deeds have carved; the diamond shines only where the cutting was true.
mirror, diamond, deeds shape you
My old teacher said that a person's deeds are cut into the face like facets in a diamond, and when I looked in the mirror after years of bitterness I saw what he meant.
doha w a needle and a furnace - each stitch of ur deeds goes into the clothes u wear later, and the furnace tests everything. karma stuff
needle, furnace, deeds sewn
The needle stitches the garment of thy fate, and the furnace tests every seam; wear what thy hand has sewn.
My grandmother, a tailor, used a needle for sixty years and said every wrong stitch comes back to you when the furnace-heat of summer shows the weak seam, and she said life is the same.
Write a doha where each deed is a stitch made by a needle into a garment that the doer must himself wear, and the furnace of time tests every seam, so we live in our own actions.
I want a doha for someone angry that bad things keep happening to them, gently reminding them that today's troubles may be returns of earlier actions and that the way out is better deeds from now on.
doha about how bad things happening might be a result of my past actions and i should do better now
Weep not at the fruit thou dost meet; change the deed, and the day will change after it.
own deeds, own results
After losing my business I blamed everyone, and then my old teacher quietly asked how I had treated my workers, and I started to see my own part in it.
doha about blame, stop blaming others for ur life, its the result of ur own choices

Write a Kabir style doha for a person who blames fate and others for his misfortune, reminding him that his actions are the cause and what he faces is only their result, so he should change his deeds.
Why curse fate and strangers? The cause was in thy hand; the result is only its echo.
My brother blames the government, his boss and bad luck for being broke, but he never saves and always spends before pay day, and I wish he could see the connection.
stop blaming, own it
My mother once put aside a single pearl from her wedding jewellery to pay for a poor girl's wedding, and in her old age that girl's family took care of her when no one else did.
Need a doha about a pearl freely given to a poor bride by a kind woman, which returns to her many times over in her time of need, to show that goodness given is goodness received in the end.
pearl given, blessing returns
The pearl given in secret to the poor returns as a necklace of blessings in the hour of need.
doha with a pearl - give something precious to someone in need and it comes back to u

Write me a doha for a businessman who has been exploiting others in secret, warning him that no profit made by hurting others stays with him, and the result of his actions will arrive to claim its due.
doha about how cheating people for money always costs u later
dishonest gain, lost
My cousin made a quick fortune by selling fake products, and three years later the lawsuits took everything he had, and my father quietly said, the account got settled.
Gain that is bought with another's tears is borrowed; the payment falls due when thou least expect it.
doha: whatever u give out in the world is what u get, positive or negative
you get what you give
As thou givest to the world, so doth the world give thee; none may take what he never gave.
I used to snap at everyone on my team, and one day my intern burst into tears and quit, and a week later three seniors followed him, and I finally saw what my tone had done.
Write a doha reminding us that the world gives back to each person according to what he gives to it, so that a person who gives love will get love and one who gives hatred will get hatred.
The fish that swallows the bait is drawn by its own hunger; the hook was only the shape of its desire.
doha w a fish - fish bites the hook cuz of its own greed, deeds bring their own results
Compose a doha about a fish that is caught by the very bait it desired, teaching that people are caught by the results of their own cravings and deeds, and that no fate is imposed from outside.
fish, greed, own fate
My uncle bought a cheap investment scheme because of his own greed and lost everything, like a fish biting a hook, and he now says it was his own deed that caught him.
My brother tied a rope around his promises and tied himself by moonlight into a pile of debts, and now says that the rope he spun for others was around his own neck.
doha w a rope and the moon - the rope u tie for others ends up round ur own neck, even the moonlit night cant hide it
The rope woven for another's neck is laid by moonlight around thine own.
rope, moon, self-bound
Could you do a doha in which a man weaves a rope to bind another but finds, in the cold light of the moon, that it coils around his own hands, teaching that harm we plan for others binds us?
Write a doha for a parent who wonders why their grown child ignores them, gently suggesting that the care and respect we show our own elders is what our children learn and later return to us.
doha on treating ur parents right cuz ur kids are watching and will treat u the same
I never visited my father in his last years because I was busy, and now my own son lives in another country and calls only on holidays, and I see how the pattern repeated.
The child learns what the elder shows; as thou treatest thy father, so shall thy child treat thee.
parents, children, returns
Write a doha about the cloud that gives rain freely to all fields and returns in the next season as a blessing to the giver, teaching that those who give without calculation are given back in full.
The cloud gives all its water to the earth, and rises again from the same earth's breath; so giving is returned.
cloud gives, returns
doha w a cloud: it gives its water and then fills up again, like good deeds coming back
My father gave free tuition to the neighbourhood kids even when we had little, and now, like a cloud returning, those children have come back to support our school, and I understand his generosity.
bridge, shroud, deeds ahead
Please give me a couplet about a man crossing the bridge to the other world in only a shroud, with his deeds as his only baggage, teaching that all that matters is what we have done and what returns.
doha w a bridge and a shroud, the only thing that crosses with u is ur deeds
When my grandfather died, wrapped in the shroud, hundreds of people came over the old bridge to say he had once helped them, and I understood what he really owned in the end.
Across the bridge of death goes only the shrouded one, and with him the deeds that were truly his.
deeds are your own
No one eats the result of another's deed; each must meet the harvest of his own hand.
Write a doha reminding us that no one else can carry the result of our deeds for us, that parents and friends cannot share our consequences, and that each person must bear what he himself has done.
My family always bails my brother out of every mess he makes, and the one time they could not, he finally had to face what he had done and began to change for the first time in his life.
doha about everyone facing the results of their own actions, no one can do it for you
Write a doha about the bee that gathers honey from flowers and finds that its own sting, used in anger, brings its death, teaching that the good we do is sweet to us and the harm we do pierces us.
The beekeeper told us that a bee that stings dies from it, and I thought of my own bitter words that I used against colleagues, which ended up costing me my own promotion.
doha w a bee: honey for the kind, sting that kills the stinger, u know karma
bee, honey, sting
The bee gathers sweetness by gentle work, and dies by its own sting; so goes every deed.
The crow that kept stealing from our neighbours' terraces finally got trapped in a wire on our roof, and my grandfather observed that what a crow takes the crow pays for.
The crow that steals what is not its own pays with what is its own; none keeps what he took.
doha w a crow stealing stuff and getting caught, the deed returns
crow, theft, returns
I'd love a doha about a crow that grabs and takes what belongs to others and is, in the end, caught by the loss of his own, teaching that theft and trickery come back upon the one who practises them.
The palanquin carries the bride of her deeds; as she has sown in the world, so she is lifted or dropped.
At my cousin's wedding the palanquin bearers refused to carry the groom's greedy father, saying they had been cheated by him years earlier, and the whole village was silent at the sight.
doha w a palanquin - who carries u depends on how u treated them
palanquin, bearers, deeds
Write a doha in which the bearers of a palanquin carry gently the one who treated them kindly and drop the one who was cruel, to show that people return to us exactly what we have given them.
doha with fire - u play with fire and get burnt, simple karma
My nephew set a small fire for fun in the neighbour's yard, and then his own bike caught fire the next week from a short circuit, and the family kept saying it was bound to return.
fire, burnt by own deeds
Write a doha in which a man lights a fire to burn another's straw and finds the wind carrying it back to his own, teaching that harm we do to others returns with greater force upon ourselves.
He who lights a fire for his neighbour's roof finds the flames at his own threshold.

I would like a doha for a young man who is tempted to take an easy dishonest shortcut, reminding him that the consequences of the deed will walk behind him and that honest effort alone brings lasting results.
doha about how shortcuts and cheating always catch up with u later
shortcuts catch up
My roommate copied his entire thesis, passed with praise, and two years later his degree was revoked on the day he was to start a new job, and I stopped taking shortcuts that week.
The easy road that goes round the labour comes back to the same gate with a heavier bill.
My neighbour kept a bird in a cage for twenty years and when he lay on his bier, I kept thinking of the cage, and that all things come back, and I let my own bird out the next morning.
The cage built for the bird becomes the bier's own enclosure; what thou bindest binds thee at last.
cage, bier, returns
Give me a doha about a man who kept creatures locked in a cage all his life and lies at last on the bier, teaching that cruelty dealt out to others returns to the one who dealt it.
doha w a cage and a bier - the one who cages others ends up caged too, at the end
Write a doha for the man who worked hard all his life for his family and was disappointed at the end, telling him that his sincere deeds will bear their results even if people forget.
doha for when u do good and nobody notices, it still counts and comes back
My father worked double shifts for decades to put us through school, and when he retired he felt unappreciated, but years later each of us began to care for him unasked, a return after a long delay.
unnoticed good deeds
The unnoticed good deed is a stream under the earth, and one day it breaks into the open.

The musk deer in the reserve was hunted for the very scent it carried, and our guide said that sometimes what we carry within becomes our fate, and our deeds are the scent that attracts our consequences.
The musk deer carries the scent that calls the hunter; so thy deeds are the fragrance that calls thy fate.
doha w a musk deer - the scent u carry draws ur fate, like ur deeds do
musk deer, own scent, fate

Write a doha in which the musk deer bears within it the very fragrance that draws the hunter to it, teaching that the deeds we carry within us attract their own consequences, and no one can escape his own creation.
your fate, your making
Not the world but thy own hand has written thy tomorrow; read it with courage and rewrite it.
My uncle spent his life complaining of bad luck, but my aunt says that his luck was just the sum of his small daily choices, and he never bothered to look at them.
A doha, please, that tells a person that his fate is not a gift or punishment from outside but only the sum of what he himself has done, and that by changing his deeds he can change what comes.
doha about how ur future is made by ur own actions not luck
The winnowing fan sifts the paras from the gravel; the deeds of a lifetime are sifted the same, and the true remains.

Write a doha in which the winnowing fan separates the true from the false in a man's life, as though sifting the paras from rubble, teaching that only the deeds that were real return to him with value.
After my father passed away, the winnowing fan he kept for the harvest reminded us that his good deeds were the paras that remained when all the husk of his life was blown away.
doha w a winnowing fan and the paras - the real deeds are what stay when the rest is blown away
winnowing fan, paras, true deeds
doha on treating people with kindness cuz it returns, someone was so kind to me when i was down
One kindness cast upon the waters of a stranger's need returns as a morning in thine own.
Write a doha for someone who is grateful that a stranger once helped them in a time of need, saying that kind deeds go out into the world and return to the giver by the roads of other people.
kindness comes full circle
When my car broke down in the dark a stranger spent two hours helping me, and later I learned he had been helped the same way by someone my father had once helped, and the circle felt complete.
doha about being honest at work, since what u do to others returns, i got a promotion cuz i helped a lot of people
Give help to those below, and the ladder will be held for thee; give none, and thou shalt climb alone.
I stayed late helping my juniors for years without credit, and this spring one of them, now a director, offered me the role I had always wanted without my asking.
help others, rise yourself
Need a doha showing that the person who generously helps others in their work will find the same help returned to him when he needs it, because every act of support flows back to the one who gave it.
